destination.name: Goulburn
destination.tagline: A heritage wool city between Sydney and Canberra, home to a 15 m concrete ram.
destination.description: Goulburn is a regional city of about 24,000 people, 200 km south-west of Sydney, and claims to be Australia's first inland city to be settled. It grew on the road south from Sydney and later on the wool trade, and was granted city status twice, in 1853 and 1885. The Hume Highway bypassed it in the 1990s, but it remains the main city between Sydney and Canberra. Visitors stop for the Big Merino and for Bungonia National Park's limestone gorge about 20 km away.
whyVisit: See the Big Merino up close
Look into Bungonia Gorge from the Lookdown

goodToKnow.title: Big Merino by the highway
goodToKnow.detail: The ram stands beside the highway service area at the southern Goulburn exit, with a bakery and fast food; stairs inside lead to a lookout at the top.

goodToKnow.title: Bungonia entry fee
goodToKnow.detail: Bungonia National Park charges an entry fee of about $8; the park is always open and the office runs 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Cold, windy winters
goodToKnow.detail: Goulburn sits in a valley with hot dry summers and cold winters (about -5 to 18 degrees Celsius); bring layers, as it can be very windy.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} avoid the valley's hot dry summers and cold, windy winters, though Wikivoyage says any season works with the right clothing.
